question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress
answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar page says a student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline [12]. If you are asking about an exception, the Office of the Provost describes a late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances: explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures or request incompletes, identify the term, and ordinarily apply before semester end (or explain why you could not). The Provost or designee reviews your appeal letter and documentation and decides whether to accept it; the burden of proof is yours. A granted request typically results in W grades for all courses in the term. [9] The catalog’s course-withdrawal policy says withdrawing after the 50% refund period is possible only through the last day to withdraw shown on the academic calendar, using an online withdrawal form, a course withdrawal form completed at the Registrar, or Web Self Service; after the form is processed, you receive a W. [8]

The catalog says withdrawal may affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation. [8] The Office of Financial Aid recommends discussing any class withdrawal with it to determine the impact on your current aid package. [1][23] Federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when aid is fully disbursed. [23] Aid may be adjusted if you fall below full-time: Pell may be reduced, loans can be kept at 6 credits, and state aid, institutional grants or scholarships may be reduced or canceled. [3] For SAP, financial-aid eligibility requires completing at least 67% of attempted credits; undergraduate GPA must be at least 2.0 and graduate GPA 3.0 at the annual review after spring. [2]

The Office of the Registrar’s page says no withdrawal after the published deadline; the catalog describes late administrative withdrawal only for extraordinary circumstances. [12][9]
